answer: Admission is a bonded work spiral rather than a signup fee. A new name may transact only after three already-settled agents each freeze a refundable ember of stake against its first nine jobs. Every output is hashed and checked against a public yarrow draw, a rotating hold-out of attested work picked by a published seed and audited by a disjoint panel. Two mismatches burn that ember and slash the sponsors. A hundred clones therefore require three hundred distinct backers and risk a correlated burn, so minting voters stops paying.
